primary_source.errata: EC3 Issue #325 rewrites Algorithm 2.B step (a) as the owner/user two-case K0 sequence; code's password‖K‖extra repetition matches it. Issue #24 removes the mistaken zero-IV phrase from ECB descriptions; AES-CBC unwrap in Algorithm 2.A retains a zero IV. Issue #542 affects §7.6.3.1's AES padding wording used by the legacy AES path; `doc/errata-read.md` records the added full-block padding behavior. No applicable correction found to §§7.6.3.2–.3 or 7.6.4.3.2–.3 beyond these references.

features.code: crates/pdf-syntax/src/crypt.rs::Encryption::object_key, encrypt_under, decrypt_under; AES object-key and data cipher helpers
features.assertions: crypt.rs unit test checks the spec's object 258/generation 7 appended bytes and an AES-only sAlT control. External producer files issue9972-1.pdf and issue17069.pdf exercise AESV2; bug900822.pdf and issue17215.pdf exercise legacy RC4. Clause-derived revision 2/3/4 fixture tests exist but independently implement the same algorithms, so external files are the independent oracle.

features.code: crates/pdf-syntax/src/crypt.rs::decrypt_under / AESV3 branch and serialize writer path
features.assertions: issue7665.pdf is an independent R6 producer witness and the R5 issue21579.pdf test embeds its producer ciphertext unchanged. R6 serialization round-trip is self-consistency only. No independent known primitive vector was rerun in this audit.

features.feature: legacy file key derivation; PDFDocEncoding/password padding, O, unsigned little-endian P, first ID, metadata sentinel, MD5 iterations and length
features.assertions: Internal boundary tests cover empty/short/long padding, Table D.3 conversion, object key and legacy owner unwrap. External R2/R3/R4 corpus documents assert successful plaintext/content decoding; generated R2/R3/R4 fixtures separately exercise flags, ID and EncryptMetadata. These assertions provide both real producer and algorithm-written evidence, with different strengths.

features.feature: R6 password preparation, owner-first/user authentication, two-case Algorithm 2.B hash, key-salt derivation and AES-CBC key unwrap
features.code: crypt.rs::utf8_password, authenticate_aes256, hash_2b, file_key_from; writer-side AES256 protection path
features.assertions: Strong independent read-side controls are present in real producer corpus files: issue7665.pdf (R6) and saslprep-r6.pdf, whose published password changes under RFC 4013 SASLprep; issue6010_2.pdf covers UTF-8 password handling. Tests assert the supplied password opens and a wrong/empty password refuses. The in-tree R6 document generator reimplements 2.B and checks user/owner passwords, but is not an independent oracle for the hash itself. No direct unit assertion was found for the RFC 4013 transform vectors or the 127-byte R6 truncation boundary; a focused helper draft is supplied.

features.assertions: Tests check serialized field lengths/structure, deterministic entropy behavior and reader round-trip. Round-trip uses the same implementation and does not independently prove every generated hash/wrapped key/filler layout. External R5/R6 producer fixtures support reader behavior, not R6 writer outputs. No independently reproduced fixed R6 writer output vector is present in reviewed tests.

features.feature: Algorithm 13 decrypts the 16-byte block, verifies adb, extracts permissions and metadata flag; Algorithm 2.A says P match is mandatory
features.code: crypt.rs::perms_block and Encryption::new: when marker validates, permissions and EncryptMetadata are replaced by decrypted values; bad marker silently leaves dictionary values
features.assertions: Current tampered-P test changes /P on a serialized R6 document and expects decrypted /Perms to win. This is a deliberately inconsistent/nonconforming input, not a valid-file conformance test. Source step 7.6.4.3.3(f) says decrypted flags 'shall match' /P; Algorithm 13 says they 'should match' /P and byte 8 'should match' EncryptMetadata. The test/ADR authority claim needs qualification; no valid-input mismatch test is warranted. Handling invalid marker/mismatch is an unresolved malformed-file policy, not a confirmed reader defect.

residuals: Potential bound discrepancy: `hash_2b` caps at 256 rounds, while 2.B has no stated fixed upper cap. From its byte-threshold condition, termination is guaranteed by round index 287; in principle a valid prepared input requiring rounds 257–287 would be truncated and fail authentication. Such vectors are cryptographically vanishingly rare under random salts and were not generated; classify as an implementation-bound risk, not a confirmed defect in this shard.
No independent R6 writer-output vector for Algorithms 8–10 was built.
No precise recovery rule for inconsistent P/Perms, metadata marker, or invalid adb marker is established; those cases are outside conforming input and need explicit policy treatment.
Deprecated writer algorithms are not treated as required PDF 2.0 output behavior; legacy read support is included because real legacy files remain in scope.
No Cargo or Git command was run. Draft is not executed.
verdict: partial-source-implementation-assertion-review; independent legacy and R6 read-side witnesses exist; R6 writer crypto has round-trip-heavy coverage; no confirmed valid-input defect
